info.title: Rask.Cli — the `rask` command-line tool
info.description: The `rask` .NET tool: a productivity front-door for the Rask framework. Scaffold a new project (`rask new`), run it with hot reload (`rask dev`), manage EF Core migrations and back the database up (`rask db`), and deploy to a single host over SSH with auto-HTTPS (`rask deploy`) — a thin wrapper over the .NET SDK. Run it with no arguments for an interactive new-project wizard. Install with `dotnet tool install -g Rask.Cli`.

commands.name: completion
commands.description: Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, or fish).

commands.name: db
commands.description: Manage EF Core migrations, and back the database up or restore it.

options.name: --project
options.description: Project containing the DbContext (default: found from the current directory).

options.name: --startup-project
options.description: Startup project (default: same as --project).

options.name: --context
options.description: DbContext to use when the project defines more than one.

options.name: --output
options.description: Migration output directory (add), or the backup file or directory to write (backup).

options.name: --remote
options.description: Act on the deployed database instead of the local one (backup, restore).

options.name: --host
options.description: Deployment host for --remote (default: the one in .rask/deploy.json).

options.name: --app
options.description: Deployed app name for --remote (default: the one in .rask/deploy.json).

options.name: --yes
options.description: Skip the confirmation prompt (drop, restore).

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print what would run without touching the database.

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON instead of a human-readable report.

arguments.name: ADD
arguments.description: Create a migration from the current model.

arguments.name: LIST
arguments.description: List the migrations and which are applied.

arguments.name: UPDATE
arguments.description: Apply pending migrations to the database.

arguments.name: DROP
arguments.description: Delete the database and everything in it.

arguments.name: BACKUP
arguments.description: Copy the database to a file.

arguments.name: RESTORE
arguments.description: Replace the database from a backup file.

commands.name: deploy
commands.description: Build and deploy the app to a single host over SSH (auto-HTTPS with --domain).

options.name: --host
options.description: SSH target to build and run on (remembered in .rask/deploy.json).

options.name: --domain
options.description: Public domain to serve over HTTPS via Caddy (implies ports 80/443).

options.name: --port
options.description: Published port when not using --domain (default: 8080).

options.name: --container-port
options.description: Port the app listens on inside the container (default: 8080; remembered).

options.name: --project
options.description: Project to deploy (default: found from the current directory).

options.name: --name
options.description: Container/app name (default: derived from the project).

options.name: --dockerfile
options.description: Dockerfile to build (default: ./Dockerfile).

options.name: --env-file
options.description: File of KEY=VALUE lines to pass to the container.

options.name: --env
options.description: Environment variable to pass (repeatable).

options.name: --health-path
options.description: HTTP path probed for readiness before the blue-green swap (default: /health).

options.name: --no-health-check
options.description: Skip the post-deploy HTTP health check.

options.name: --github-actions
options.description: Write a .github/workflows/deploy.yml that runs this deploy on push, and print the secrets to add.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the docker commands that would run without changing anything.

options.name: --json
options.description: Print the result as JSON instead of a human-readable report.

options.name: --tail
options.description: Log lines to show (logs only; default: 100, 'all' for everything).

options.name: --follow
options.description:
Stream new log lines until interrupted (logs only).
Host setup options (first deploy to a box):

options.name: --setup-host
options.description: Prepare the host without asking (installs Docker, creates the deploy user, firewall, SSH hardening).

options.name: --no-setup-host
options.description: Never change the host; fail with instructions if it isn't ready.

options.name: --deploy-user
options.description: Non-root login to create and deploy as when given a root host (default: deploy).

options.name: --no-deploy-user
options.description: Keep deploying as the --host login instead of creating a non-root one.

options.name: --no-firewall
options.description: Don't configure ufw on the host.

options.name: --no-harden-ssh
options.description: Don't disable SSH password login and root login on the host.

arguments.name: ACTION
arguments.description:
Operate on what's already deployed instead of deploying (omit to deploy).
Actions:

arguments.name: STATUS
arguments.description: Show what is running, and on which color.

commands.name: dev
commands.description: Run the app with hot reload (dotnet watch).

options.name: --project
options.description: Project to run (default: the project in the current directory).

options.name: --urls
options.description: URLs the app should listen on (sets ASPNETCORE_URLS).

options.name: --launch-profile
options.description: launchSettings profile to use.

options.name: --open
options.description: Open the app in your browser once it is listening.

options.name: --no-open
options.description: Never open a browser.

options.name: --no-hot-reload
options.description: Restart on change instead of applying edits live (still watches).

options.name: --no-restart
options.description: Ask before restarting on an edit hot reload can't apply.

options.name: --once
options.description: Run once without watching (plain 'dotnet run').

options.name: --no-banner
options.description: Suppress the startup banner.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Print the command that would run without starting anything.
